clue.text: Please take, so to speak, French abstracts

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read as letters

parts.note: please is PRAY and take is SEIZE, so the pair are spoken as 'pray seize'

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks to be handed summaries written in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of this French loanword is spelt the same but said 'pray-seez', which is exactly how 'pray seize' sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is borrowed from French and means short summaries, so it names abstracts with a French origin.

clue.text: What doctor has to do when in charge

definitions.text: What doctor has to do when in charge

parts.words: What doctor has to do when in charge
parts.note: a doctor in charge runs a surgery business, and also must do a professional job; both senses name the same word

explanation.surface: Describes the duties of a doctor running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's business is called by this word, and doctors carry on their profession.

clue.text: Gradual reduction, or is one mistaken?

indicators.note: mistaken says the letters of the preceding words are wrongly arranged and must be sorted

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a slow decline is their own error.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing away little by little, as of soil or rock, is a slow decrease.

clue.text: Where stock may be put with some difficulty

definitions.meaning: stock is broth, which goes into a bowl of broth-based food
in trouble, an idiom

explanation.surface: Shares might be placed only with trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' wants to be shares; it is cooking broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is added to a liquid dish; the idiom for being in trouble uses the same phrase.

clue.text: Deceives? It could look like double-cross

definitions.meaning: cheats on, especially by being unfaithful to two partners at once
a times sign is a cross, so two of them side by side look like a double cross

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is pictorial: the multiplication sign × is a cross, and two of them make a 'double cross', which also echoes deceiving.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat on a lover is a betrayal; written as signs, ×× is a pair of crosses.

clue.text: It shows what's in store for the man in the street

definitions.text: It shows what's in store for the man in the street

parts.words: It shows what's in store for the man in the street
parts.note: read literally, a shop's display shows passers-by what goods are inside

explanation.surface: Something reveals the ordinary person's future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's in store' sounds like the future; it means goods inside a shop, shown to passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging goods in a shop's front display lets passers-by see the stock.

clue.text: List of numbers put on board

definitions.meaning: a chart of figures, such as a multiplication chart
to place a proposal before a committee for discussion

explanation.surface: Figures are written up on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of figures in rows; also, in British usage, to present a motion for debate.

clue.text: Passion? Maiden is first to go wrong

indicators.note: first says the maiden and is come at the front, before the passion

parts.note: in cricket a maiden over is abbreviated M
passion is ardour or fire

explanation.surface: Passion leads a young woman astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' looks like a young woman; it is the cricket over abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: When a gun or plan fails to work properly it fails to fire as intended.

clue.text: Southern Irish lake or wet area

parts.note: lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A lake in the south of Ireland or a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern Irish lake' looks like one phrase; Southern gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp or bog is a muddy, waterlogged place.

clue.text: Breeding displayed in 46, for example

definitions.meaning: reproduction, increasing in number
4 across and 6 down together make the name of a chart learnt by schoolchildren showing the products of numbers

explanation.surface: A breed shown in some numbered entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The '46' is a cross-reference: 4 across plus 6 down make the schoolroom chart of times sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals breeding increase their numbers; the arithmetic operation fills a times chart.

clue.text: Military command executed 4 to restore position

definitions.meaning: an order on the parade ground to turn and face the opposite way
4 across is a phrase meaning twice; doing this half-turn twice brings a soldier back to facing the original way

explanation.surface: A drill order carried out a couple of times puts a soldier back where they began.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' is a cross-reference to 4 across, read here as 'two times': two half-turns make a full circle.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade, the order to swivel and face the rear is a standard drill instruction.

clue.text: One employed in club as soloist?

definitions.text: One employed in club as soloist?

indicators.note: employed in says the letters are put to work inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A performer is hired by a club to sing on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the run 'club as soloist' contains the word, and the whole clue describes an Italian-styled low-voiced singer giving a solo.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian term names a singer with the lowest male voice, who often takes solo parts.

clue.text: Weapon a copper was impressed with

definitions.meaning: a three-pronged spear
the old British penny, a copper coin, was stamped with Britannia holding a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: A policeman was struck by some kind of arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a policeman; it is the penny coin, and 'impressed' means stamped, not admiring. Britannia, Britain's emblem, held this spear on old pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune's three-pronged fishing spear counts as a weapon, and it appeared in the design on the penny.

clue.text: One of these batsmen is removing cap

definitions.meaning: in cricket the first pair to bat are called by this adjective
taking the top off a bottle or jar

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the top of the order takes off his cap.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the two batsmen who start an innings are described by this word; uncapping a bottle is the same word as a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's first two batsmen are the start of the innings; unscrewing a lid is unsealing the jar.

clue.text: Fit for nothing, is unable to start

indicators.note: to start says the inability comes at the beginning, ahead of the nothing

parts.note: is unable means can't, written without the apostrophe
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone useless has no idea how to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is not healthy here but an old word for a section of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic sense of fit is a division of a long poem, the same as a section of an epic.

clue.text: Lear's old man in a tree was part of his

definitions.text: Lear's old man in a tree was part of his

parts.words: Lear's old man in a tree was part of his
parts.note: evokes Edward Lear's limerick about an Old Man in a tree, but an old man in a family tree is an ancestor, part of someone's line of descent

explanation.surface: Edward Lear's nonsense character up a tree belonged to his lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote a limerick beginning 'There was an Old Man in a tree'; the tree here is a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorded line of ancestry is a family tree, on which an old forebear sits.

clue.text: The way to Samarkand — not a flower in sight

indicators.note: not says the following letter a is to be left out

parts.note: from James Elroy Flecker's poem 'The Golden Journey to Samarkand' and its line about the gilded road there

explanation.surface: Along the route to Samarkand there is no flower to be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a flower in sight' reads as a barren road; 'not' removes A, and 'flower' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-plumed plant of the daisy family is a garden flower.

clue.text: So fast it's not pursued, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is identified by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: not chased after

explanation.surface: Someone moving so quickly is not followed, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' wants to mean quick; it means immoral, loose in behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of fast is promiscuous, lacking sexual restraint.

clue.text: Altered, perhaps, about one stone

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the single letter
altered tells us the letters of the next word are changed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a gem has maybe been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' turns PERHAPS into SAPPHRE, and 'about' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue gemstone of the corundum family is a precious stone.

clue.text: Virtuous, like Disraeli's side?

definitions.meaning: pure, saintly
Disraeli declared himself 'on the side of the angels' in the evolution debate

explanation.surface: A politician's party is described as morally good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a political party; Disraeli, Victorian prime minister, said he was 'on the side of the angels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly behaviour is heavenly, the quality of the hosts of heaven.

clue.text: Quarter from which omnibus came

parts.note: points to a district of Paris and to the language that gave us the word omnibus, meaning 'for all'

explanation.surface: A bus came out of one district of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paris district is the Left Bank student area; 'omnibus' is a word from the ancient language of Rome, so it 'came from' there.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Roman language names both the Paris student district and the source of the word for a bus.

clue.text: Man put up, in fashion, as supporter

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the fashion word

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A man raised fashionably to be a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is the old sense 'the ton', high society's style; 'put up' reverses in a down clue. A telamon is a column carved as a man.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture, a column carved as a male figure holds up a structure.

clue.text: Got ready for female no gentleman embraces

indicators.note: embraces means the cad holds the female inside

parts.note: a man who is no gentleman is a cad
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman prepares for a rogue who hugs her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash: to have got ready money is to have turned a cheque into money.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Ready' is slang for money, so converting a cheque into money is getting ready.

clue.text: Girl harboured in Sicily

definitions.meaning: a woman's given name
a port town on Sicily's east coast

explanation.surface: A young woman was given shelter on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harboured' wants to mean sheltered or hidden; it means 'is a harbour', the Sicilian port of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name and also a seaport on the eastern coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Hanging South American native for sin

definitions.meaning: a slow tree-dwelling mammal of South America that hangs upside down
laziness, one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A South American native is hanged for wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests execution; it is the animal's upside-down habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow mammal hangs from branches; idleness is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Secrecy as the last resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it says the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Keeping things quiet is what someone falls back on when all else fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last resort' looks like a phrase; 'resort' is re-sort, rearranging THE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by stealth means doing something covertly, keeping it hidden.

clue.text: Meeting, it's said, gets a full house

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Meeting, it's said, gets a full house (5)' as printed: 'Meeting, it's said' defines the greeting, but no reading found ties 'gets a full house' to the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: Meeting, it's said, gets a full house

clue.text: Fool heads off Italian and French author

indicators.note: heads off means each of the two following words loses its first letter

parts.note: an Italian gentleman is a signor
Albert Camus was a French author

explanation.surface: A clown dodges an Italian and a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' looks like a verb meaning intercepts; it beheads both SIGNOR and CAMUS, leaving IGNOR and AMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant, stupid person is a dunce or fool.

clue.text: Pack one's share of it for sailor

parts.note: a pack of cards is a deck
the cards dealt to one player from the pack are a hand

explanation.surface: Someone packs their portion of something for a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a verb; it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A crewman who works on the ship's deck is a sailor.

clue.text: Port after duck is by no means rare

indicators.note: after places the thick part following the nought

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nought, O
rare can mean thin, as in rarefied air, so its opposite is thick

explanation.surface: Port wine taken after a duck dinner is very common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like wine; it is a Danish port city. 'Rare' is thin air, not uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Danish island of Funen is a harbour town.
